module_title: Rare Instruments, South Indian Maestros, and Grammy Winners
introduction: When SSC wants to make a shift particularly difficult (Hard level), they ask about South Indian percussion instruments (Ghatam, Mridangam) and rare North Indian instruments (Surbahar, Pakhawaj).

core_concepts.title: Ghatam (Ghana / Solid Instrument)
core_concepts.description:
Exponents: **T.H. Vinayakram** (also known as 'Vikku'), E.M. Subramaniam.
Key Fact: A Ghatam is essentially a large, specially baked clay pot, played with the hands and fingers. T.H. Vinayakram is a Grammy Award winner.

core_concepts.title: Pakhawaj (Avanaddha / Percussion)
core_concepts.description:
Exponents: **Pt. Bhavani Shankar**, **Totaram Sharma**, Pt. Ayodhya Prasad.
Key Fact: It is an ancient, barrel-shaped, two-headed drum. It is the predecessor of the Tabla and is mainly used to accompany 'Dhrupad' style singing.

core_concepts.title: Mridangam (Avanaddha / Percussion)
core_concepts.description:
Exponents: **T.K. Murthy**, Palghat Mani Iyer, Umayalpuram K. Sivaraman.
Key Fact: The Mridangam is the primary rhythmic accompaniment in Carnatic (South Indian) classical music.

core_concepts.title: Other Important & Rare Instruments
core_concepts.description:
1. **Surbahar:** **Annapurna Devi** (Daughter of Ustad Allauddin Khan). It is also known as the 'Bass Sitar'.
2. **Rudra Veena:** Ustad Asad Ali Khan.
3. **Saraswati Veena:** S. Balachander, Doraiswamy Iyengar.

important_entities.name: Bharat Ratna Awardees in Music
important_entities.significance: A highly favored SSC trivia topic. The recipients are: 1. M.S. Subbulakshmi (1998), 2. Pt. Ravi Shankar (1999), 3. Ustad Bismillah Khan (2001), 4. Lata Mangeshkar (2001), 5. Pt. Bhimsen Joshi (2008), 6. Bhupen Hazarika (2019).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: Because she was Pt. Ravi Shankar's first wife and Allauddin Khan's daughter, students often assume she played the Sitar or Sarod. Her actual instrument was the rare **'Surbahar'**.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Lord Vinayak (Ganesha) is depicted with a pot belly. A Ghatam is literally a clay pot. Therefore, T.H. 'Vinayak'ram plays the Ghatam.

exam_strategy_tips: A frequent question in SSC CGL Tier 1 & 2: 'Grammy award winner T.H. Vinayakram is associated with which musical instrument?' Answer: Ghatam.
